sections.title: What actually transfers when you leave Xero
sections.body: Switching accounting systems requires planning. You cannot simply press a button and move everything. You can export your customer lists, vendor details, and inventory items from your current system and import them into Paper & Pen. However, historical transactions and closed invoices do not transfer automatically. The most practical approach is to pick a clean cutover date, usually the start of a new financial year or quarter. You will need to export your trial balance from your old system on the final day, then enter those closing balances as opening balances in Paper & Pen.
items: Export your customer and supplier contact lists
Download your chart of accounts and item lists
Choose a clean cutover date for new transactions
Enter your closing balances as new opening balances

sections.title: What you gain when you make the switch
sections.body: Paper & Pen provides a different approach to business software. Instead of a mandatory monthly subscription for basic accounting, our core sales and invoicing features are free forever. You get full access to create estimates, proforma invoices, credit notes, and recurring invoices without hitting a paywall. You also gain multi-currency support and configurable tax rates out of the box. Because we offer paid add-on modules for human resources, payroll, and manufacturing, the system grows with you. You only pay for complex operational tools when your business actually requires them.
items: Free forever core invoicing and sales tools
Multi-currency support and configurable tax rates
Five interface languages including right-to-left Arabic
Paid modules for HR and manufacturing available

sections.title: When keeping your current software makes sense
sections.body: We want you to use the right tool for your business. Xero is established accounting software with a paid subscription, and it excels in specific areas. If your external accountant works exclusively in Xero and refuses to use other systems, you should weigh that heavily before moving. Furthermore, Xero is strong on automatic bank feeds and bank reconciliation. Paper & Pen does not offer automatic bank imports. If daily automated bank reconciliation is critical to your operations, you are better off staying where you are. Please check their official website for their current plans and pricing.
items: Your accountant requires you to use Xero
You rely heavily on automated bank feeds
Daily automated bank reconciliation is strictly necessary
You depend on their third-party app marketplace

faqs.q: Can I import my historical invoices into Paper & Pen?
faqs.a: No. Moving historical transactions between different accounting systems is highly complex and prone to errors. We recommend keeping a read-only export of your historical data from your previous software for compliance purposes. You should start fresh in Paper & Pen by entering your opening balances and creating new invoices from your chosen cutover date.

faqs.q: Does Paper & Pen connect to my bank account?
faqs.a: No. We do not offer automatic bank feeds or open-banking integrations. You will need to manually enter your payments and expenses, or upload manual journal entries to keep your ledgers up to date. If automated bank imports are a strict requirement for your business, you should consider staying with your current provider.

faqs.q: How does the pricing compare to Xero?
faqs.a: Paper & Pen offers core invoicing, sales, and basic accounting features completely free forever. We do not charge a monthly subscription for these fundamental tools. We generate revenue through optional paid modules for human resources, payroll, and manufacturing. For current pricing and plan details regarding Xero, please visit their official website.

faqs.q: Can my accountant access my Paper & Pen account?
faqs.a: Yes. You can invite your accountant to your workspace so they can review your ledgers, post journal entries, and generate profit and loss statements or balance sheets. However, you should have a conversation with your accountant first to ensure they are willing to work outside of their preferred software ecosystem. Some accountants only support specific platforms, which is a valid reason to stay with your current provider.
